purpose: The world section of the-reefer.com: the same kind of plain answers as the state pages, for other countries, plus a travel warning list. Every answer names its sources and the date it was checked. A missing answer means not yet reviewed.

questions.label: Can adults use it without a prescription?
Where can adults buy it legally?
How much can an adult carry?
Can adults grow it at home?
Can an old cannabis record be cleared?
Can you take it across the border?

CA.name: Canada
CA.summary: Legal for adults nationwide since October 17, 2018. Provinces set the age, who sells it and some home-grow rules.

adult-use.short: Yes. 18 federally, 19 in most provinces, 21 in Quebec
adult-use.detail: Federal law sets 18 as the minimum and lets provinces raise it. Ontario, British Columbia and Manitoba use 19, Alberta uses 18 and Quebec raised its age to 21 on January 1, 2020.
adult-use.citation: Cannabis Act (S.C. 2018, c. 16); provincial government pages

medical.detail: Medical cannabis stays under Health Canada, separate from the provincial rules for non-medical cannabis.
medical.citation: Government of British Columbia; Government of Ontario

buying.detail: Buy from a retailer authorized by your province. Where a province has no retail system, adults can buy online from federally licensed producers. Ontario's online store (OCS.ca) supplies the province's authorized stores.
buying.citation: Department of Justice Canada; Ontario Cannabis Store

possession.detail: Adults can carry up to 30 grams of legal dried cannabis, or the equivalent, in public. British Columbia also caps what a household keeps at home at 1,000 grams.
possession.citation: Department of Justice Canada; Government of British Columbia

sharing.short: Up to 30 grams with another adult
sharing.detail: Adults can share up to 30 grams of legal cannabis with other adults.

home-grow.detail: Federal law allows 4 plants per residence, from licensed seed or seedlings. Quebec bans home growing, and the Supreme Court of Canada upheld that ban in 2023. Manitoba ended its ban on May 1, 2025 and now allows 4 plants per household for people 19 and older.
home-grow.citation: Cannabis Act; Murray-Hall v. Quebec, 2023 SCC 10; Government of Manitoba

border.detail: Cannabis cannot be taken into or out of Canada, including to or from US states where it is legal. This is a federal offence under the Cannabis Act.

driving.short: Criminal THC limits: 2 ng and 5 ng
driving.detail: Having 2 to under 5 nanograms of THC per millilitre of blood within two hours of driving is a less serious criminal offence; 5 ng or more is more serious; and 2.5 ng combined with a blood alcohol of 50 mg per 100 ml is also an offence. There is no medical exemption. Some provinces add zero tolerance: Newfoundland and Labrador allows no detectable THC for novice drivers, commercial drivers and anyone under 22.
driving.citation: Criminal Code and Blood Drug Concentration Regulations; Justice Canada; Government of Newfoundland and Labrador

record-relief.short: Free record suspension for old possession convictions
record-relief.detail: Since August 1, 2019, people convicted only of simple possession of cannabis can apply to the Parole Board of Canada for a record suspension with no fee and no waiting period, without a lawyer. Non-Canadians convicted in Canada can apply too. A record suspension sets the conviction aside but does not erase it, and it does not guarantee entry to another country.
record-relief.citation: Parole Board of Canada; Public Safety Canada

differences.title: What is different about Canada
points: Legal nationwide under one federal law since October 17, 2018, with each province adding its own rules.
The legal age depends on the province: 18 in Alberta, 21 in Quebec, 19 everywhere else.
Each province picks its own store model: government-run, private, or a mix.
Quebec bans home growing, and the Supreme Court upheld that in 2023.
Old possession convictions are set aside by a free record suspension, not erased by expungement.
You still cannot cross the border with it, in either direction.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.summary: Illegal for recreational use. Cannabis is a Class B drug. Specialist doctors have been able to prescribe cannabis-based medicines since November 1, 2018, mostly through private clinics.

adult-use.short: No. Cannabis is a Class B drug
adult-use.detail: Possession carries up to 5 years in prison, an unlimited fine, or both. Supply and production carry up to 14 years.

possession.short: Warning or £90 on-the-spot fine for small amounts
possession.detail: Police in England and Wales can give a warning or an on-the-spot fine of up to £90 for cannabis; repeat offences can go up to the maximum. In Scotland, police can issue a Recorded Police Warning for possession instead of reporting it to the prosecutor; the warning still goes on the person's criminal record.
possession.citation: GOV.UK, Drugs penalties; Crown Office (COPFS); Police Scotland via STV News

medical.detail: Since November 1, 2018, cannabis-based products for medicinal use can be prescribed in England, Wales and Scotland, but only by doctors on the General Medical Council's Specialist Register. Smoking them stays illegal, even with a prescription. GPs cannot start a prescription. Since January 2026, national police guidance approved by the National Police Chiefs' Council tells officers in England and Wales how to deal with prescribed patients.
medical.citation: Home Office Circular 018/2018; Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001 reg. 16A; APCDLO guidance; Chambers 2026 (secondary)

buying.detail: There is no legal sale outside a prescription.

home-grow.detail: Growing cannabis is production under the Misuse of Drugs Act, with a maximum of 14 years in prison.

driving.short: 2 micrograms of THC per litre of blood
driving.detail: It is an offence to drive with more than 2 µg/L of THC in your blood, whether or not your driving was affected. The limit is set low on a zero-tolerance approach.
driving.citation: GOV.UK, Changes to drug driving law; Road Traffic Act 1988 s. 5A

record-relief.detail: There is no process to erase a cannabis conviction. Under the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974, a simple caution is spent immediately and a conviction becomes spent after its rehabilitation period. Spent records no longer show on a basic DBS check, but can still show on standard or enhanced checks.
record-relief.citation: GOV.UK, Rehabilitation periods; Disclosing your criminal record

experiment.text: CBD is legal to sell as food only under Food Standards Agency rules. The FSA advises healthy adults to take no more than 10 mg of CBD a day, has set a safe upper limit of 0.07 mg of THC a day, and in September 2026 recommended the first CBD food authorisations to ministers. All CBD products must still comply with the Misuse of Drugs Act.

differences.title: What is different about the United Kingdom
points: Recreational use is a crime, yet medical cannabis has been legal since 2018. One 2026 estimate puts UK patients at about 80,000 to 90,000, most of them through private clinics rather than the NHS.
Prescribed flower has to be vaporised. Smoking it is a crime even with a prescription.
Scotland handles small possession through Recorded Police Warnings set by the Lord Advocate; England and Wales use warnings and £90 fines.
The drug-driving limit for THC is 2 µg/L of blood, among the lowest anywhere.
Old convictions are never erased. They become spent and disappear from basic checks only.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.summary: No legal market. The Supreme Court struck down the total ban on personal use in 2021, but Congress never passed a law, so adults need a permit from COFEPRIS, the federal health regulator, to grow and use their own. Selling is still a crime, and tourists get no protection.
MX.note: Most official sources are in Spanish. Answers summarize them in English.

adult-use.detail: On June 28, 2021 the Supreme Court's full bench struck down the parts of the General Health Law that banned recreational use outright. Congress never wrote a replacement law. COFEPRIS says the ruling only lets an adult use cannabis personally under its health authorization, and does not legalize a market.
adult-use.citation: SCJN Comunicado 187/2021; COFEPRIS statements reported July 2026 (news)

buying.detail: There are no legal shops. COFEPRIS has stated that the court rulings do not authorize selling or distributing cannabis.

possession.short: 5 grams is the line in the health law
possession.detail: Under article 478 of the General Health Law, prosecutors do not charge a user who carries no more than the article 479 table amount, which is 5 grams of cannabis. Above that, possession can be charged as narcomenudeo. In February 2026 the Supreme Court protected one man caught with about 14 grams for personal use, but the ruling applied only to his case; the vote fell short of the majority needed to change the rule for everyone.
possession.citation: Ley General de Salud arts. 478 and 479; SCJN, Amparo en Revisión 132/2025; El Cronista (news)

home-grow.detail: A permit lets an adult acquire, plant, grow, harvest, prepare, possess and carry cannabis for personal use only. In 2026 the Supreme Court ordered COFEPRIS to issue permits it had refused, and said the paperwork can be required but cannot be used as a barrier to the right.
home-grow.citation: SCJN Comunicado 097/2026; SCJN case synopsis, Sep 2026; La Razón (news)

medical.detail: The medical cannabis regulation under the General Health Law was published in the Diario Oficial on January 12, 2021. It covers production, research, manufacturing and medical use, with prescriptions and licenses overseen by COFEPRIS.
medical.citation: Reglamento published in the DOF, January 12 2021

driving.short: No driving high; in Mexico City, 20 to 36 hours in jail
driving.detail: Traffic rules are set locally. In Mexico City, article 50 of the traffic regulation bans driving under the influence of narcotics or psychotropics, with an administrative arrest of 20 to 36 hours that cannot be paid off as a fine, plus six license points.
driving.citation: Reglamento de Tránsito de la Ciudad de México art. 50, via ADN40 (news)

border.short: Never bring cannabis in, even medical
border.detail: The U.S. government warns that drug possession and use, including medical marijuana, is illegal in Mexico and may lead to a lengthy jail sentence.

differences.title: What is different about Mexico
points: Personal use became a right through the courts, not Congress. The Supreme Court ruled in 2021, and lawmakers never followed with a law to regulate it.
The right is real but runs through paperwork. You apply to COFEPRIS for a permit, and people refused have gone back to court to force it to issue one.
There is still nowhere legal to buy. The permit covers growing your own and nothing else.
Without a permit, the 5 gram table in the health law is what separates a user from a dealer. A 2026 attempt to scrap that limit for everyone fell one vote short.
Visitors get none of this. The U.S. government warns that any drug possession, medical cannabis included, can mean a long jail sentence.

DE.name: Germany
DE.summary: Legal for adults since April 1, 2024, without shops. Adults can carry some, grow a few plants at home, or join a non-profit cultivation club.

adult-use.detail: The Cannabis Act took effect on April 1, 2024. Since then, adults in Germany can legally use cannabis.

buying.detail: Cultivation associations have been allowed to grow since July 1, 2024 and may pass cannabis only to their members. Members get at most 25 grams a day and 50 grams a month; members aged 18 to 20 get at most 30 grams a month, with no more than 10 percent THC.
buying.citation: Federal Ministry of Health FAQ; Federal Government FAQ

medical.short: Yes, under the Medical Cannabis Act
medical.detail: Since April 1, 2024 cannabis is no longer listed under the narcotics law. Medical cannabis is governed by its own law, the Medizinal-Cannabisgesetz (MedCanG).
medical.citation: Federal Ministry of Health, Cannabis als Medizin

border.detail: Bringing cannabis into Germany from abroad remains prohibited.

possession.short: 25 grams in public, 50 grams at home
possession.detail: Adults may carry up to 25 grams in public and keep up to 50 grams at home. Going a little over (up to 30 grams out, up to 60 grams at home) is a fine. Beyond that it is a crime with up to three years in prison.
possession.citation: Federal Government FAQ; Lower Saxony state government

home-grow.detail: Adults may grow up to three plants at home for their own use. The plants and harvest must be protected from children, teenagers and other people.
home-grow.citation: Federal Ministry of Health, Feb 23 2024; Federal Government FAQ

driving.short: 3.5 ng/ml THC in blood serum; zero for new drivers
driving.detail: Since August 22, 2024 it is an offence to drive with 3.5 ng/ml of THC or more in blood serum. The standard penalty is a 500 euro fine and a one-month driving ban; mixed with alcohol, the standard fine is 1,000 euros. Drivers on probation and anyone under 21 face a total ban, with a standard 250 euro fine. Patients taking prescribed cannabis are exempt.
driving.citation: StVG § 24a (BGBl. 2024 I Nr. 266); Legal Tribune Online; Deutsches Ärzteblatt

record-relief.short: Old convictions can be erased on request
record-relief.detail: Since January 1, 2025, a person convicted under the old narcotics law for something that is no longer a crime can ask the public prosecutor to confirm that the entry can be erased from the federal criminal register. The prosecutor then tells the register to delete it. Lawyers say it is unclear which entries qualify.
record-relief.citation: KCanG §§ 40 and 41; CanG Art. 15; Legal Tribune Online (news)

experiment.text: A federal evaluation called EKOCAN is running until 2028. Its second interim report, on April 1, 2026, found that cultivation clubs still play only a minor role in pushing back the illegal market; the health minister called the law a dud. A separate bill to stop telemedicine prescriptions and mail-order delivery of medical cannabis flower was introduced in December 2025 and was still in Parliament at our last check.

differences.title: What is different about Germany
points: Legal to have and grow, but there are no shops. The only legal sources are your own three plants, a non-profit club, or a prescription.
Where you light up matters. No smoking within 100 metres of the entrance to schools, playgrounds, youth centres or public sports grounds, and none in pedestrian zones between 7am and 8pm.
The clubs have been slow to start. Only 366 had been approved nationwide by October 31, 2025.

Medical cannabis became the easy route instead. Imports of medical flower rose 170 percent from the first to the second half of 2024 as online prescription platforms spread, and the government now wants to restrict them.
Driving has a hard number: 3.5 ng/ml of THC in blood serum, and zero for new and young drivers.
Old convictions for things that are now legal can be wiped from the federal register on request.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.summary: Cannabis is still illegal under the Opium Act, but since the 1970s the state has tolerated small-scale use and sales in licensed coffeeshops. Growing for those shops was never allowed; a state experiment with licensed growers started in 2025.
NL.note: Dutch sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.detail: Possessing, selling and growing cannabis are all offences. Prosecutors do not pursue adults for small personal amounts, and coffeeshops that follow the national rules are left alone.

buying.short: Coffeeshops, 5 grams per person per day
buying.detail: A coffeeshop may sell no more than 5 grams per person per day, keep no more than 500 grams in stock and admit only residents of the Netherlands. Whether the residents-only rule is enforced differs from town to town, and each town decides whether to allow coffeeshops at all.

possession.short: Up to 5 grams is not prosecuted
possession.detail: The Public Prosecution Service does not prosecute people for possessing no more than 5 grams of cannabis.

home-grow.short: Illegal, but 5 plants are not prosecuted
home-grow.detail: The government says growing cannabis at home or anywhere else is not permitted. Its toleration policy still says prosecutors do not pursue people for no more than five plants. Police can seize the plants.
home-grow.citation: Government of the Netherlands; DutchNews.nl, 2011 Supreme Court ruling (news)

medical.detail: Since September 1, 2003, pharmacies have been able to dispense medicinal cannabis to patients with a doctor's prescription. The government's Office of Medicinal Cannabis supplies standardized, pharmaceutical-grade cannabis, and every Dutch pharmacy can dispense it.
medical.citation: Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research (2018); Al Jazeera, Sep 1 2003 (news)

driving.short: 3 micrograms of THC per litre of blood; zero if combined
driving.detail: Driving under the influence of drugs is prohibited. Since July 1, 2017 there have been fixed blood limits for the most common drugs; for THC the limit is 3 µg per litre of blood. Using several drugs, or drugs with alcohol, triggers a zero limit. Police screen with a saliva test and confirm with a blood test. Two convictions in five years cancel your licence.
driving.citation: Government of the Netherlands; Netherlands Forensic Institute; CBR

experiment.text: The Controlled Cannabis Supply Chain Experiment entered its experimental phase on April 7, 2025, which fixes its end date at April 7, 2029. Coffeeshops in the participating towns may now buy, sell and stock cannabis only from designated growers, and the 500 gram stock limit does not apply to them. Before the experiment ends, the government will decide the future of coffeeshop policy based on the research.

differences.title: What is different about the Netherlands
points: Nothing about cannabis is actually legal. The famous Dutch model is a written promise by prosecutors not to act, under rules known as AHOJG-I: shops may not advertise, sell hard drugs, cause nuisance, admit minors or sell large quantities, and must serve residents only.
The back door problem: coffeeshops may sell, but growing is illegal, so for decades their supply came from the illegal market. The state experiment is the first attempt to fix that.
Tourists can be turned away. Coffeeshops are meant for residents of the Netherlands, though towns decide how strictly to enforce it.
Medical cannabis has been sold in ordinary pharmacies since 2003, earlier than almost anywhere else.
Driving uses a fixed blood limit for THC, with zero tolerance for mixing drugs or drugs and alcohol.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.summary: The first country to regulate the whole market, under Law 19.172 of December 2013. Citizens and permanent residents register for one of three routes: grow at home, join a club, or buy at a pharmacy. Tourists are shut out.
UY.note: Spanish sources are summarized in English.

adult-use.short: Yes, for registered citizens and residents
adult-use.detail: Law 19.172 regulated home growing, cannabis clubs and pharmacy sales, the first country to do so. Users must register with IRCCA, the national cannabis regulator, and can use only one of the three routes at a time.
adult-use.citation: Ley 19.172 (IMPO guide); EUDA; Pardal et al. (research)

buying.short: Pharmacies: 10 grams a week, 40 a month
buying.detail: Pharmacy sales began on July 19, 2017. Registered buyers may purchase up to 10 grams a week and no more than 40 grams a month, in sealed packs, at prices set by IRCCA. Clubs must have between 15 and 45 members and are licensed and inspected by IRCCA.
buying.citation: Decreto 120/014; IMPO guide to Ley 19.172; EUDA; Ámbito (news)

home-grow.short: 6 plants and 480 grams a year per household
home-grow.detail: Registered home growers may keep up to six flowering plants per household, with a harvest of no more than 480 grams a year, for personal or shared use at home.
home-grow.citation: IMPO guide to Ley 19.172; Government of Uruguay

driving.short: Zero alcohol, and no driving after cannabis
driving.detail: Uruguay's traffic law bars driving with any alcohol in the blood. The cannabis law also bars driving with THC above the permitted level, and the national drug board says drug use must be zero whenever you are going to drive. The government bought 1,000 drug detection devices and trained traffic officers across the country to use them.
driving.citation: Ley 18.191 art. 45; Junta Nacional de Drogas; Infobae 2014 (news)

border.detail: Only citizens and permanent residents can register, so tourists cannot legally buy. In 2026 IRCCA's director said this pushes visitors to the illegal market and that the regulator is designing a way to let them buy.

experiment.text: As of April 30, 2026, 120,083 people were registered: 88,955 pharmacy buyers, 20,798 club members and 10,330 home growers. A government evaluation in 2026 found that 46 percent of consumers now buy through the legal market, and described a remaining gray market made up mostly of unregistered home growers and informal sharing.

differences.title: What is different about Uruguay
points: The state runs it. IRCCA licenses the growers, sets pharmacy prices, registers every user and inspects clubs.
You pick one route. Home grow, club or pharmacy, never two at once.
Your pharmacy has it, maybe. Sales are at ordinary pharmacies that opt in, and in 2017 only 16 of about 1,200 did.
Pharmacy buyers are by far the largest group, almost 89,000 of about 120,000 registered in 2026.
The first legal country is closed to tourists, though the regulator now wants to change that.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.summary: The first country in Asia to decriminalize, in 2022, and the first to pull back. Since June 26, 2025 cannabis flower is a controlled herb, sold only against a prescription. A bill to make cannabis medical-only went to Parliament in September 2026.

adult-use.detail: The government says cannabis is not fully legal. Under the Ministry of Public Health's 2025 notification on controlled herbs, cannabis flower may be bought and sold only with a medical prescription. The narcotics board says a prescription can cover no more than 30 days.
adult-use.citation: Government statement via Thairath; ONCB via The Nation (news)

medical.short: Yes, by prescription from one of seven professions
medical.detail: Licensed shops may sell only to patients with a valid prescription from one of seven recognized practitioners, including medical doctors, Thai traditional medicine doctors, pharmacists and dentists. Since January 2026, every operating dispensary must have a licensed practitioner on site.
medical.citation: Tilleke & Gibbins (law firm); The Nation; Thaiger (news)

buying.short: Licensed shops, prescription only, and shrinking
buying.detail: Shops still trade under three-year licences that expire between 2026 and 2028. The health minister has said more than half of them will need to become medical facilities to renew. More than 7,000 shops have already closed as the rules tightened.

border.detail: It is illegal to carry cannabis out of Thailand, and British travellers have been caught doing it, including while transiting. Smuggling carries up to 10 years in prison, and since June 2026 bringing cannabis in can mean up to 10 years and a fine of up to 500,000 baht.

experiment.text: On September 22, 2026 the cabinet approved a draft Cannabis and Hemp Act that would limit cannabis strictly to medical use, require shops to operate as medical facilities and phase out recreational sales. It now goes to the House. In October 2026 the prime minister also proposed tougher penalties through changes to the Narcotics Act.

differences.title: What is different about Thailand
points: Thailand dropped cannabis from its narcotics list in 2022, the first Asian country to do so, and dispensaries spread fast, drawing tourists from countries with tough laws.
Since June 26, 2025 the flower is a controlled herb rather than a narcotic. It is not legal for fun, but it is regulated under traditional medicine law rather than drug law.
Walk-in sales are over. Shops may sell only against a prescription, and they are being pushed toward becoming clinics.
The shop count is collapsing as licences expire, with more than 7,000 closures so far.
Leaving with it is the biggest risk. Travellers have been caught carrying it out, and smuggling carries up to 10 years.

MT.name: Malta
MT.summary: The first EU country to legalize personal use, in 2021. No shops: adults can grow at home or join a licensed non-profit association.

adult-use.detail: Chapter 628 of Malta's laws (2021) created ARUC, the Authority for the Responsible Use of Cannabis, to allow restricted, regulated access instead of criminal enforcement.

possession.short: 7 grams carried; up to 4 plants at home
possession.detail: Adults may carry up to 7 grams and grow up to four plants at home under the 2021 law. Smoking in public is banned.

buying.detail: Supply comes from non-profit Cannabis Harm Reduction Associations licensed by ARUC. Only Malta residents aged 18 and over can join. Association possession rules were updated in February 2026.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.summary: Since January 1, 2026, adults 21 and older can grow three plants and keep 100 grams at home. No sales and no clubs yet.

adult-use.detail: A criminal code reform that took effect January 1, 2026 lets adults 21 and over grow and possess limited amounts. Commercial activity is still not permitted.

possession.short: 100 grams at home, 25 grams in public
possession.detail: Possession of 101 to 200 grams at home is an administrative offence; more than 200 grams is a crime.

home-grow.detail: Growing up to three plants is legal. Four or five plants is a misdemeanour, and more than five is a felony.

buying.detail: No retail sales, and cannabis clubs are not yet legal.

ES.name: Spain
ES.summary: Not legal, but private use and private growing are not crimes. Hundreds of private cannabis clubs operate in a legal gray zone that courts and police are tightening.

adult-use.short: Private use is not a crime
adult-use.detail: Using and growing for yourself in private is not criminal. Buying, carrying or using in public is an administrative offence with a fine and confiscation.

buying.detail: Sale and import of any amount are criminal offences that can bring prison.

home-grow.detail: Plants visible from the street or a balcony count as a serious administrative offence, with fines from €601 up to €30,000.

experiment.text: Spain's cannabis social clubs are private, members-only associations that rely on the legality of private use and shared cultivation. Their status depends on the case, the judge and the region, and a 2026 study describes their decline after years of growth. Advertising and recruiting tourists are not allowed.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.summary: Decriminalized all drugs for personal use in 2001. Possession of up to 10 days' supply goes to a health-focused panel, not a court. Selling and growing are still crimes.

adult-use.detail: Since July 2001, using, buying or possessing up to a 10-day supply of any drug is an administrative matter. Cases go to a regional Commission for the Dissuasion of Drug Addiction, which can recommend treatment, warnings or fines.
adult-use.citation: Law 30/2000; U.S. OJP fact sheet; UNSW

possession.detail: A 2008 Supreme Court ruling made possession above the 10-day amount a crime again.

buying.detail: Dealers, traffickers and growers still face criminal penalties.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.summary: Illegal above 1% THC, except for about 10,000 adults in official city pilot trials. Parliament is working on a law for regulated access.

adult-use.detail: Recreational use of cannabis with 1% THC or more stays prohibited outside the authorized pilot trials. About 10,400 adults were in the seven ongoing trials as of June 2025.

buying.short: Pilot trial pharmacies and shops only
buying.detail: The trials sell regulated cannabis to registered participants. The Bern, Biel and Lucerne pharmacy trial has been extended to October 2028.

experiment.text: A National Council committee drafted a Cannabis Products Act that would give adults legal, strictly regulated access, and sent it out for consultation until December 1, 2025. It is not law yet.

IL.name: Israel
IL.summary: One of the world's largest medical programs per person, with more than 100,000 licensed patients. Recreational use is illegal but mostly handled with fines.

medical.detail: The Israeli Medical Cannabis Agency at the Ministry of Health, set up in 2011, licenses patients and the whole supply chain. More than 100,000 people hold medical licences.

adult-use.detail: Using cannabis without a licence violates the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance. Since April 2019, people caught using in public with no previous record cannot be arrested but can be fined up to 1,000 shekels.

experiment.text: In May 2026 a Health Ministry committee recommended phasing out smoked medical cannabis in favor of extracts or precision inhalers.

travel_warnings.detail: Possession of even very small quantities can lead to the death penalty, according to UK travel advice. Singapore classes cannabis as a Class A drug, with up to 10 years in prison and a fine of up to S$20,000 for consumption. Drug use detected on arrival can mean arrest.
Zero tolerance. Possessing, using, making or trafficking drugs can bring long prison sentences or the death penalty. Airports scan transit passengers' bags for cannabis.

Possession, trafficking and manufacture of any illegal drug, including cannabis, are serious offences. British travellers have been caught carrying cannabis while only transiting. Australia lists Malaysia among countries that apply the death penalty to drug offences.

Possession is a crime outside a COFEPRIS permit, and visitors have no permit. The U.S. government warns that drug possession and use, including medical marijuana, is illegal in Mexico and may result in a lengthy jail sentence.
UAE authorities treat drugs found in your bloodstream as possession, so use before arrival can lead to charges. Some CBD products are illegal.
Since December 12, 2024, using cannabis is a crime. Possession, use and transfer each carry up to 7 years in prison, and import carries 1 to 10 years.
Possession or use can bring up to 5 years in prison, and smuggling carries much longer terms, followed by deportation and an entry ban (Thai embassy warning).

travel_warnings.risk: Up to 10 years at the border
travel_warnings.detail: Since June 2026, bringing cannabis across Thailand's border can mean up to 10 years in prison, a fine of up to 500,000 baht, or both.
Australia's government lists these among countries that apply the death penalty to drug offences.

texas_concentrates.text: In Texas, THC concentrates (vape oil, wax, most edibles) are not treated as marijuana. They are Penalty Group 2 controlled substances, and possessing less than 1 gram is a state jail felony: 180 days to 2 years and a fine of up to $10,000.
texas_concentrates.citation: Tex. Health & Safety Code 481.103 and 481.116; NORML penalty table
